description: Hi everyone! I'm passionate about space science, technology, and problem-solving. My background includes coding, data analysis, and creative brainstorming. I'm looking to build an enthusiastic and diverse team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to tackle exciting global challenges together. We are currently looking for members with skills in programming, graphic design, research, or science communication. Let's create something amazing!
summary:
Here is a comprehensive summary of the "Space Relik" project in English, written in a paragraph format:
"Space Relik" is an interactive space museum application designed specifically for children aged 9 to 13 to spark their passion for space exploration and astronomy through engaging digital experiences. The project addresses the decline of interest in space among youth caused by traditional, complicated, and uninspiring learning methods. To solve this, the app guides users through four progressive levels—each featuring five historical tools left behind by NASA in space—combining visual exploration with interactive quizzes that users must pass to advance. Upon completing all levels, users tackle a final major mission (such as assisting in a rocket launch) to evaluate their success rate, and they are ultimately rewarded with a personalized certificate of achievement celebrating their accomplishment.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works:

Space Relic is an interactive web-based space museum and mission simulator for kids aged 9 to 13. Players explore 4 progressive levels, each featuring 5 real NASA tools (20 tools total) explained in simple language. After every level, players pass a quick quiz to unlock the next gallery. Finally, they complete a hands-on Space Mission using the tools they learned and receive a Mission Success Rate (%).

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Space science often feels boring to kids because traditional resources are too technical and non-interactive. Space Relic turns passive readers into active junior explorers, sparking curiosity, reinforcing learning through play, and encouraging friendly competition—all accessible via any browser with zero downloads.

Creativity:

Our project uniquely combines visual museum exploration, progressive quizzes, and a practical mission simulation, helping kids understand how real NASA tools solve actual space challenges.

Tools, Languages & NASA Data:

• NASA Open Data: NASA Image & Video Library (for authentic visuals) and NASA TechPort (for accurate tool functions).

• Tech Stack: Built as a web app using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React, with UI design in Figma.

Factors Considered:

We focused on age appropriateness (9–13) by simplifying complex engineering terms, scientific accuracy using official NASA data, and accessibility through a lightweight browser-based platform
